confirmed.title: 'iz' mode: Temizle / Geri al do not reset the traced-path progress, so dots stay lit and a fresh drawing finishes itself early
confirmed.scenario: A 3-year-old in iz mode scribbles messily and covers about 85% of the dotted path, then taps Temizle to start clean. The paper empties but every lit dot stays painted. The coverage counter also stays at 85%. The child draws one neat first line, the counter passes 93%, and the screen auto-jumps to sonuç after 650 ms with only that one line drawn: low stars and a 'something is missing' message. The idle finger hint also skips lines it still thinks are 'filled', so after a clear it can point at the wrong line or not appear at all.
confirmed.evidence: const dolu = new Uint8Array(noktalar.length); let sayi = 0; (296-297) are only ever set (dolu[i]=1; sayi++; daireler[i].classList.add('dolu')) and never cleared. The Temizle/Geri al buttons (439, 441) call tuval.temizle()/tuval.geriAl(), which just fire onDegisim. onDegisim (368) does `if (!bos && tamamMi() && !bitiyor) ... setTimeout(bitir, 650)` with tamamMi = () => sayi / noktalar.length >= 0.93 (308). bostaKur's hint (324) reads the same stale dolu.
reasons: CONFIRM: I couldn't refute it. The bug can be reached in the shipped app. 'iz' is a real mode, and the app picks it by default for age 3 and under (resimler.ts:434 `if (!yas || yas <= 3) return 'iz'`). When there is no nokta game, the Temizle and Geri al buttons (ekranlar.ts:439, 441) call tuval.temizle() and tuval.geriAl() directly. In src/ui/tuval.ts:60-69 those methods only change the stroke list and then call this.onDegisim(). Nothing resets the closure state `dolu`/`sayi` (ekranlar.ts:296-297). The only code that writes to them is geriBildirim, and it only ever sets values (dolu[i]=1; sayi++; classList.add('dolu')). The lit circles in `boyali` are never un-classed either. The guards don't stop this. Right after Temizle, `bos` is true, so the auto-finish is skipped for that one call. When the next stroke ends, onDegisim runs again (tuval.ts:57). Now bos is false, tamamMi() reads the stale `sayi` (still at or above 0.93), and bitiyor is false. So setTimeout(bitir, 650) fires, and bitir only refuses to finish when the paper is empty (377). The idle hint at line 324 also reads the stale `dolu`. So the scenario matches the code: after a clear, the dots stay lit, and one new line can finish the drawing early.

CONFIRM: I could not refute it. The bug is real and reachable in 'iz' mode. In canlan/src/ekranlar.ts, `dolu` and `sayi` (lines 296-297) are only ever increased, inside geriBildirim (lines 301-304). Nothing ever clears them, and the 'dolu' class is never removed from `daireler`. Temizle and Geri al (lines 441 and 439) call tuval.temizle()/tuval.geriAl() in src/ui/tuval.ts (lines 60-70). Those only change `cizgiler`, redraw and call onDegisim, so the lit dots and the coverage count from the wiped strokes stay. After a clear, onDegisim (line 368) checks `tamamMi()` (`sayi/noktalar.length >= 0.93`, line 308) against that stale count. One later stroke only has to light the remaining ~8% of dots to set off `setTimeout(bitir, 650)`. bitir then sends only the strokes still on the canvas (line 384) to puanla, which gives few stars. The idle hint (line 324) reads the same stale `dolu`, so it skips lines that are no longer drawn. No comment, ORTAK_NOTLAR entry or test says this is intended, and no guard resets the state. There is one small correction: a neat line that only traces over dots already lit adds nothing to `sayi`, so the early finish happens only if the new stroke reaches dots that were not lit before. The dots still look painted on a blank paper either way, which misleads the child.

CONFIRM: I could not refute this. The bug is real and users would see it. Tuval.temizle() and geriAl() (src/ui/tuval.ts:60-70) only change `cizgiler`, redraw the canvas and call onDegisim. In iz mode, `dolu` and `sayi` (canlan/src/ekranlar.ts:296-297) only ever go up in geriBildirim (299-307). Nothing ever sets them back. onDegisim (361-373) does not recompute them. The Temizle and Geri al buttons (439, 441) call tuval directly whenever `nokta` is null, which is always true in iz mode. Two visible effects follow. (1) The lit dots are drawn on the separate `ust` overlay SVG and have class `dolu`, which canlan.css:623 shows at opacity 0.55 in the picture's colour. So after Temizle the paper still shows a coloured traced path the child didn't just draw, an obvious "clear didn't work" moment. (2) `sayi` keeps its old value, so tamamMi() (308) can pass 0.93 after only a few fresh strokes. Then the auto-finish at line 368 fires and bitir() sends only the new lines to sonuç, giving a poor result for a nearly empty drawing. One detail in the scenario is off: redrawing lines that were already lit adds nothing, because the `!dolu[i]` guard skips them. So reaching 93% after a clear needs only the small leftover of uncovered dots (e.g. clear at 90%, then a short stroke over unlit dots is enough). It is still very reachable. The idle finger hint (324) also reads the stale `dolu`, so it skips lines that were drawn before the clear.

confirmed.title: Closing jingle plays after leaving the moral card: it lands on the catalog or cuts off the next film's intro music
confirmed.scenario: The film ends and the moral card appears while the narrator is still reading it. The child taps "Tekrar izle" (watch again) or "Çizgi Filmler" right away. About 0.4 s later the film-kapanis jingle starts. If the child went to the catalog, it plays over the catalog screen. If they tapped Tekrar izle, it cross-fades out the new film's film-acilis intro music, so the intro runs with the wrong music.
confirmed.evidence: ogutKarti does `void konus(metin).then(() => kapanisJenerigi(0.4), () => kapanisJenerigi(0.4))`. Uygulama.git() first calls sus(), which resolves the pending konus promise (kayitDurdur→calanBitti / tekParca bitir), then calls the old screen's kapat(), which runs `zamanlar.forEach(clearTimeout)`. The .then runs in a microtask after that, so kapanisJenerigi→sonra() pushes a fresh setTimeout into the already-cleared `zamanlar` array. Nothing clears it, so it fires `filmMuzik.dosyaCal({ad:'film-kapanis'})`, and dosyaCal calls dosyaDur(gec, true) on whatever file music is playing. There is no closed/alive flag on the film screen.
reasons: CONFIRM: I could not refute it. The bug happens for real users. In ogutKarti (film/src/ekranlar.ts:88), the "Tekrar izle" and "Çizgi Filmler" buttons are added to the card at once, while konus(metin) is still reading the moral. Tapping either one calls Uygulama.git (src/uygulama.ts:72). git first calls sus() (src/audio/konusma.ts:50). sus() runs kayitDurdur(), which takes calanBitti and calls it, so the kayitCal promise resolves true. It also runs bitir?.(), which resolves tekParca. If the narration was still fetching its buffer, kayitCal resolves through iptalMi(). If the konusma setting is off, a 250 ms timer resolves it. So every path resolves the konus promise. Then git calls eski.kapat(). That runs zamanlar.forEach(clearTimeout) and filmMuzik.dur(0.5), all inside the same click handler. The async IIFE and the .then(() => kapanisJenerigi(0.4)) only run as microtasks after that. So sonra() pushes a new setTimeout into a zamanlar array that has already been cleared, and nothing clears it again. The film screen has no alive/closed guard. filmMuzik is a module singleton. When the timer fires, dosyaCal({ad:'film-kapanis'}) does several things: it calls muzikDurdur(), so any other music stops; it raises ana gain back to 1; it calls dosyaDur(0.05, true), which fades out every playing file track, including a new film-acilis; and it starts the jingle through this.duck. That path skips cikis, whose gain dur() had set to 0, so the jingle is audible. On "Tekrar izle", the new screen opens with oynat:true, and its acilis akis calls dosyaCal('film-acilis') once the images decode (cached) or after 1.5 s at most. That is about the same moment as the stray film-kapanis 0.4 s later, so the two cross-fade over each other. The only case that is safe is when the card is not read aloud (sonSoz === metin, or sessiz/TEST mode). There kapanisJenerigi is scheduled synchronously, so kapat's clearTimeout catches it.

CONFIRM: I could not refute it. The bug happens for real users. In film/src/ekranlar.ts:88, `konus(metin).then(() => kapanisJenerigi(0.4), ...)` has no check that the screen is still open. A child can tap the buttons while the narrator is still reading, because tekrar/liste are added to the card at the same moment the speech starts (lines 77-82). Uygulama.git (src/uygulama.ts:72-78) runs `sus()` and then `eski.kapat?.()` synchronously. sus() resolves the pending speech: kayitDurdur fires calanBitti, and `bitir?.()` resolves tekParca (src/audio/konusma.ts:50-62, 138-147). Even without that, tekParca's emniyet timeout would resolve it later. Either way, the konus async function and its .then run as microtasks after kapat() has already done `zamanlar.forEach(clearTimeout)` (line 140). kapanisJenerigi then calls sonra(), which pushes a new setTimeout into the array that was just cleared, and nothing clears it again. After 0.4 s, `filmMuzik.dosyaCal({ad:'film-kapanis'})` runs. dosyaCal (film/src/muzik.ts) has no alive or stopped flag. filmMuzik.dur(0.5) in kapat does not stop it. dosyaCal also calls muzikDurdur() and `dosyaDur(0.05, true)`, which fades out every file music that is playing. So on "Tekrar izle", the new screen's acilis film-acilis track (film/src/acilis.ts:201, dosyaCal at open) is cut off and replaced by the closing jingle. On "Çizgi Filmler", the 5 s jingle plays over the catalog. The comment "konuşma sesi iptal edilirse de çözülür" means the jingle should still play if speech fails on the same screen. It does not show any intent to play it after the screen is gone, and the result (wrong music over the next film's intro) is clearly not what was intended. It only happens with sound on (`!sessiz && !TEST_MODU`), so tests never hit it, but users do.

CONFIRM: I traced the claim through the code and it holds. In ogutKarti (film/src/ekranlar.ts:88), the closing jingle waits for `konus(metin).then(() => kapanisJenerigi(0.4))`. When the child taps a button, Uygulama.git (src/uygulama.ts:75-78) calls sus() first. sus() runs kayitDurdur(), which calls calanBitti and settles the kayitCal promise right away (kayit.ts:128,156-158), and it also calls bitir() for TTS (konusma.ts:60). The async body in konus resumes only in later microtasks, so the outer promise and the `.then` run after git() has finished, which includes the old screen's kapat() doing `zamanlar.forEach(clearTimeout)`. kapanisJenerigi then calls sonra(), which adds a new setTimeout to the already-cleared `zamanlar` array. Nothing clears it again and there is no closed/alive flag. 0.4 s later it calls filmMuzik.dosyaCal({ad:'film-kapanis'}), and dosyaCal checks nothing about which screen is active. It calls muzikDurdur(), turns the music bus back up to 1, and dosyaDur(0.05, true) fades out any file music that is playing. User impact. (1) "Çizgi Filmler": a 5 s closing jingle plays over the catalog, and any catalog background music is stopped. (2) "Tekrar izle": app.git('film',{oynat:true}) calls basla() right away. acilis.ts:201 starts film-acilis as soon as the cached images decode, usually well within 0.4 s. The leftover timer then cross-fades the intro music into the closing jingle (gec 0.05). The intro, timed to the beats of film-acilis, runs with the wrong music. Kids often tap while the moral is still being read, so this path is easy to hit, and a parent or reviewer would hear a clearly wrong sound. Small but real. I am not refuting it.

confirmed.title: Pause then resume starts the synth 'nese' theme under the mp3 score in sentez:false films
confirmed.scenario: Fresh app session, watching Kino ve Oyuncak Sepeti, Sıra Bende, Lütfen or Mino'nun Sepeti (all `"sentez": false`). The child taps pause and then Devam, or the app goes to the background (auto-pause) and the child taps Devam on return. From then until the film ends, the Web Audio synth tune plays on top of the film's mp3 music. Same root cause in Kino ve Elma Kulesi scene 3: after the scripted `muzik dur` silence, a pause/resume brings the synth music back during the sad scene.
confirmed.evidence: duraklat(false): `if (!this.c || !this.cikis) return; ... else if (!this.bitis) { this.cikis.gain.setTargetAtTime(0.9,...); this.zaman = ...; this.devam(); }`. `cikis` already exists because the intro's dosyaCal('film-acilis') called zincir(). `bitis` is false unless a 'kapanis' synth theme has finished, and `ruh` defaults to 'nese'. Nothing checks FilmDosya.sentez or whether the synth was running before the pause. devam() starts setInterval(planla) and plays TEMA[this.ruh] into cikis.
reasons: CONFIRM: I could not refute it. The bug happens for a real user, in both the app build and the website. Call path: the Oynat tap runs basla(), which calls acilisKur with muzik: MUZIK (true outside test mode). Its akis() calls filmMuzik.dosyaCal({ad:'film-acilis'}) (film/src/acilis.ts:201). dosyaCal calls zincir() (film/src/muzik.ts:179), and that creates this.cikis with gain 0.9. The scene file-music events (motor.ts:749) do the same. Then Film.oynat skips baslat() because dosya.sentez === false (motor.ts:393). So the synth never ran, but cikis exists, bitis=false and ruh='nese'. Pausing, either with the Duraklat button (ekranlar.ts:41-47) or by auto-pause through arkaPlanDinle (ekranlar.ts:52), calls Film.duraklatDegistir, which calls filmMuzik.duraklat(d) (motor.ts:418). this.muzik = secenek.muzik ?? !TEST_MODU is true, because the Film constructor is not given a muzik option. Tapping Devam calls duraklat(false): the guard `!this.c || !this.cikis` passes, and the `else if (!this.bitis)` branch ramps cikis back to 0.9 and calls devam(). devam() starts setInterval(planla), which plays TEMA['nese'] into cikis, then duck, then ana; ana gain was set to 1 by dosyaCal. Nothing checks sentez or whether the synth was running before the pause, so the synth plays over the mp3 score. The four sentez:false films are confirmed: content/film/kino-kaydirak.json, kino-lutfen.json, kino-oyuncak.json and mino-sepet.json. The 'muzik dur' case is also real: dur() (muzik.ts:284-287) only stops the timer and fades cikis; it never sets bitis, so a later resume restarts the synth. The only thing that stops it is a finished 'kapanis' theme setting bitis.

CONFIRM: The bug is real and it goes against what the docs say should happen. FILM-REHBERI.md says that `"sentez": false` means the film does not start the synth music (nese…). motor.ts:393 follows this and skips `filmMuzik.baslat` when `sentez === false`. These four films set `sentez: false`: kino-oyuncak, kino-kaydirak, kino-lutfen and mino-sepet.

Here is the path. Starting the film calls `filmMuzik.dosyaCal('film-acilis')` (acilis.ts:201), or the film's own `dosya` music events (motor.ts:749). Both call `zincir()`, which creates `cikis` with gain 0.9. `bitis` stays false because the 'kapanis' synth theme never ran, and `ruh` defaults to 'nese'.

Pausing goes through ekranlar.ts:41-53: either the Duraklat button, or `arkaPlanDinle`, which auto-pauses when the app goes to the background. That calls `Film.duraklatDegistir` → `filmMuzik.duraklat(d)` (motor.ts:418). The `this.muzik` flag there defaults to `!TEST_MODU`, so this runs for real users.

On resume, `duraklat(false)` in muzik.ts:268-279 passes the `!this.c || !this.cikis` guard. It then takes the `else if (!this.bitis)` branch: it sets `cikis` gain to 0.9 and calls `devam()`. That starts `setInterval(planla)`, which plays `TEMA['nese']` notes into `cikis` (connected at lines 366/380/401/416), on top of the mp3 score.

Nothing checks `sentez` or whether the synth was playing before the pause. No guard, comment or test shows this is intended. The child hears two pieces of music clashing until the film ends, which goes against the rule the docs state.

CONFIRM: I couldn't refute it. The bug happens for real users and you can hear it.

1. **The guard only covers film start.** motor.ts:393 skips the synth only when the film begins: `if (this.muzik && this.dosya.sentez !== false) filmMuzik.baslat('nese')`.
2. **The music object is already set up.** The intro calls `dosyaCal('film-acilis')` (acilis.ts:201), which calls `zincir()`, so `this.c` and `this.cikis` exist. `ruh` defaults to 'nese' and `bitis` is false.
3. **Pause and resume both reach the synth.** motor.ts:418 `duraklatDegistir` calls `filmMuzik.duraklat(d)` on every pause and resume. The automatic pause when the app goes to the background (ekranlar.ts:52) uses the same path, so this is common and needs no unusual taps.
4. **Resume starts the synth with no check.** muzik.ts:268 `duraklat(false)`, under `else if (!this.bitis)`, sets the gain to 0.9 and calls `devam()`, which starts `setInterval(planla)`. Nothing checks `sentez` and nothing checks whether the synth was playing before the pause.
5. **The affected films never use the synth.** content/film/kino-oyuncak.json, kino-lutfen.json, kino-kaydirak.json and mino-sepet.json all set `"sentez": false`. Their only music events are `dosya` and `dosya-dur`, with no `baslat` or `ruh`, so any synth sound in them is wrong.
6. **The 'muzik dur' case is real too.** `dur()` never sets `bitis` either, so a pause and resume after a scripted silence brings the synth back.

**Impact:** a looping C-major plucked tune (104 bpm, shaker) plays at gain 0.9 on top of mp3 scores played at about 0.55. It is a second song in a different key and tempo, playing until the film ends. A parent or a store reviewer would clearly hear it.

confirmed.title: Paused film's mp3 music/song plays on when the AudioContext resumes (app back from background, tapping the sound button); song then out of sync with karaoke
confirmed.scenario: A film with mp3 music is playing, e.g. Kino ve Sihirli Söz's 'Lütfen' song with karaoke. The parent switches apps: the film auto-pauses through arkaPlanDinle. On return the film stays frozen with the Devam button showing, but the scene music or song keeps playing. The same happens when someone taps the sound button while the film is paused, because efekt.dokunma→baglam() resumes the context. When Devam is tapped, the song has moved ahead of the frozen karaoke and film timeline.
confirmed.evidence: Pause depends only on suspending the shared context: `if (this.c && this.dosyalar.length) void (d ? this.c.suspend() : this.c.resume())`, and cikis gain→0 mutes only the synth. File sources are wired `src.connect(g).connect(this.duck!)`, which bypasses cikis. The context is resumed by other code with no film-pause check: src/kabuk/yerel.ts arkaPlan(false) resumes every context that was running before the background, src/audio/motor.ts visibilitychange calls ctx.resume() when visible, and baglam() calls `if (ctx.state === 'suspended') void ctx.resume()` on every effect. confirmed.scenario: In the key 'tidying is a game' scene, Kino flips each cube (kup-mavi, kup-sari, kup-kirmizi) up, grabs it and kicks it into the basket. reasons: CONFIRM: I traced the path and it is reachable for a user, so I could not refute it. The film 'kino-oyuncak' is listed in the shipped catalog (film/src/katalog.ts:23, marked yeni). In scene 4-topla, k1, k2 and k3 have the types kup-kirmizi, kup-sari and kup-mavi (content/film/kino-oyuncak.json around line 1882). CONFIRM: I could not refute the claim. The cubes really do disappear while Kino carries them.

1. The pick-up path runs in the shipped film. olayYap 'al' (motor.ts:918) calls this.al(). kino-oyuncak is the first entry in katalog.ts SIRA, marked yeni:true. content/film/kino-oyuncak.json uses film "kino-oyuncak" with malzeme "ev", and its scene 4 has 'al' and 'birak' events on k3, k2 and k1, which are of type kup-mavi, kup-sari and kup-kirmizi.

No kup*.webp exists in any of them; the only kup.webp in the repo is assets/ege/kup.webp. 3. So motor.ts:1000 passes ''. Oyuncu.al then calls tasi() (oyuncu.ts:448-466), which adds an SVG `<image href="">`. That draws nothing, and there is no fallback to the SVG placeholder.
